Question: Measurement–valve relation of a P loop
Expected from the control law alone: Exact under controller-input and broken under post-update recording (Eqs. (1) and (2))

Question: Effect after separate relearning and calibration
Expected from the control law alone: Not determined; relearning may absorb the added noise
Observed: Fault 9: 98.2% and 14.6% detected within 40 h, at FARs of 3.65% and 6.25%; on all 52 variables, 94.4% and 59.5% (Table 2). Faults 3 and 15: mainly within 8 h for family A and at all horizons for family B; with SFA, Fault 15 only (Fig. 3; Table 3)

Question: Measurements that carry the effect
Expected from the control law alone: Not determined; the control law shows which measurement–valve relations break, not which measurements carry detection
Observed: Added normal variance of the fixed family A monitor: mostly XMEAS12, XMEAS15 and XMEAS17 (Section 4.1). Detection in the exchange tests of the fixed-template autoregressive monitors: for Faults 3 and 9, not these three (+0.5 and −3.1 pp) but the other 19 (+90.2 and +65.0 pp), mainly XMEAS2; for Fault 15, XMEAS17; with XMEAS17 already exchanged, also exchanging the two level measurements had little additional effect on 8 h detection (at most 4 pp); the D-feed flow controller uses a setpoint written by the outer composition loop, the stripper-underflow controller an integral term (Supplementary Section S6; Fig. 4)

Question: Monitoring the Fault 15 loop alone
Expected from the control law alone: Its integral term is read exactly from a controller-input record; whether this suffices for detection is not determined
Observed: A linear readout, XMV11 + G·XMEAS17, detected at most 2.4% of the runs of any fault within 8 h (Supplementary Table S26)

Question: D-feed state in a post-update record
Expected from the control law alone: Recoverable from the recorded history of XMEAS26 with the outer control law, its initialization and the sampling phase; effect on detection not determined
Observed: Controller-input XMEAS2 recovered within 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁰ kg h⁻¹ in the 7,248 runs used for Faults 3 and 9; detection within 8 h 97.2% for Fault 3 (controller-input record, 99.3%) and 44.4% for Fault 9 (63.4%), within 40 h 96.9% (99.4%) (Section 4.6; Fig. 5)

Question: Normal variation along learned directions
Expected from the control law alone: Smaller under controller-input recording where a direction cancels the noise carried by a valve output; size not determined
Observed: Template directions trained on controller-input records: normal projection variance 0.80% (Fault 3) and 1.63% (Fault 9) of its post-update value, fault displacement nearly equal; on directions trained on post-update records, 1.85 and 1.74 times (Supplementary Section S13)
